title: The Divine Warrior
aka: the LORD's march from the south
lead: In a group of old poems the LORD marches from the south (Sinai, Seir, Paran, Teman) at the head of armies, and the earth, sea and mountains break before him. The pattern runs from Exodus 15 through Judges 5, Deuteronomy 33, Psalm 68 and Habakkuk 3.

sections.b: The poems share a pattern: the LORD sets out from the south, nature shakes, the sea or river is defeated, the enemies are scattered, and the people are rescued (Exodus 15:1-18; Judges 5:4-5; Deuteronomy 33:2; Psalm 68:7-8; Psalm 77:16-20; Habakkuk 3:3-15). Frank Cross traced the pattern to the poetry of Canaan and early Israel. The Bible keeps the vocabulary and gives it to one God. In the New Testament the image returns at the Lord's coming (Revelation 19:11-16).
